extracted.intended_audience: mystery writers, publishers, television writers/producers, and industry observers interested in the Edgar Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Explain how the Edgar Awards operate, including category structure, submission procedures, and eligibility rules for works in fiction, nonfiction, short fiction, juveniles/YA, and television. Useful for authors, publishers, and producers deciding whether and how to enter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-judged awards (committee composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edgars are "peer awards" judged by "volunteer committees of professional writers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is conducted by volunteer professional writers rather than public voting or a single editor. This signals recognition from within the profession and shapes expectations about criteria and prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edgar Award categories (scope of eligible work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards cover Best Novel, Best First Novel, Best Paperback Original, Best Fact Crime, Best Critical / Biographical Work, Best Short Story, Best Juvenile, Best Young Adult, Best Episode in a TV Series, plus named and special honors (Robert L. Fish, Sue Grafton, Mary Higgins Clark, Lilian Jackson Braun, Grand Master, Ellery Queen, Raven Award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Edgars span a wide range of genres and formats—novels, debuts, paperback originals, nonfiction, criticism/biography, short stories, children’s and YA, and television—plus special awards for lifetime achievement and service. Entrants should identify the single category that best fits a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal submission process (entry forms required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must submit work to the relevant category through formal entry forms rather than casual recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are structured and administrative: follow the entry form instructions exactly. Failure to use the proper entry form can prevent consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate entry per work and mailing requirements (TV example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate entry form must accompany each work submitted; television entry form instructs entrants to mail works to each committee member for the appropriate category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each work requires its own paperwork and, at least for TV, physical or direct mailing to committee members. Treat each entry as an independent submission and confirm delivery procedures for the category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited submission materials and judge contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are explicitly warned not to include reviews or other promotional materials and not to contact the judges directly; direct contact could make a submission ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not append press clippings, marketing materials, or attempt to influence judges. Contacting judges or including promotional items risks disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitted vs. nominated distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearing on the MWA submissions list does not mean a work has been nominated; it means only that the work has been submitted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate being entered with being shortlisted or nominated; communications and publicity should reflect the actual status listed by MWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-content policy for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 TV entry form requires entrants to confirm that the submission’s substantive content is free of AI-generated material; limited assistive uses such as copyediting, grammar checking, or formatting support are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core narrative, thematic development, and stylistic choices must reflect the author's own creative work. Minor AI-assisted tasks (grammar, formatting) are permitted, but reliance on AI for substantive creative content risks ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe (publication/production year)
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards honor work from the previous calendar year; the 2026 awards recognize work published or produced in 2025, and TV works must have been released or aired in the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the exact calendar-year window for the relevant Edgar cycle and ensure publication/airdate falls within that year to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-committee submission rule (category exclusivity) and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of certain named awards, a work may be submitted to only one Edgar committee. Exceptions identified include the Robert L. Fish Award, Sue Grafton Memorial Award, Mary Higgins Clark Award, and Lilian Jackson Braun Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants and publishers must choose the single committee/category that best fits a work rather than submitting the same title to multiple competitive categories; certain named awards can be additional avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published works ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-published works are not currently eligible for Edgar Award consideration (MWA membership and eligibility guidance states this directly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who self-publish should be aware they cannot enter under current rules; pursuing traditional/qualifying publishers or the approved-publisher route is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Edgar consideration, a short story must be published by an MWA-approved publisher and the author must have received at least $25 for the story before the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short story is not Edgar-eligible merely by existing or being published somewhere; it must meet both the approved-publisher and minimum-payment thresholds by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an MWA-approved publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: The approved-publisher rules say the publisher must have paid a minimum of $500 to at least five authors in the mystery/crime genre who have no financial or ownership interest in the company; MWA maintains an approved publisher list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the current MWA approved-publisher list and the publisher's payment history/status before attempting a short-story submission. The rule is designed to ensure a professional publishing standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/professional standards over popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edgars are structured field awards run by the leading professional organization for mystery writers; they are not fan-voted popularity prizes nor loose 'best of year' lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect criteria and selection processes to reflect professional norms and peer judgment rather than sales figures or popular voting; positioning, industry recognition, and adherence to submission rules matter.
